\hypertarget{the-unchanged-target}{%
\subsection{The unchanged target}\label{the-unchanged-target}}

For odd \(N\ge3\), use raw modular Weyl operators

\[
(T_N(a,b)\psi)(x)=e_N\bigl(b(x+2^{-1}a)\bigr)\psi(x+a),
\qquad e_N(t)=\exp(2\pi i t/N),
\]

with modular inverses. Let \(S=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}3&4\\2&3\end{smallmatrix}\right)\) and

\[
(M_N)_{xy}=N^{-1/2}e_N\bigl(-8^{-1}(3x^2-2xy+3y^2)\bigr),
\qquad U_N=\exp(i\tau N A_N)M_N,\quad \tau=10^{-80}.
\]

Here \(A_N\) quantizes \(f-1/10\) using \(e^{2\pi i(kq+lp)}\mapsto T_N(l,k)\),
where

\[
\begin{split}
r(q)&=(1-\cos14\pi q)(1+\cos2\pi q),\\
f(q,p)&=\cos14\pi q+\frac{r(q)}{10}
 +\frac{r(q)\sin2\pi q}{100}
 +\frac{r(q)\cos(2\pi p-\alpha_0)}{100},\\
e^{i\alpha_0}&=(-3+4i)/5.
\end{split}
\]

Centering changes only a common spectral rotation. Neither an auxiliary
coupling average nor independent phases replace this fixed family.

Writing \(p_m=\operatorname{Tr}U_N^m\), the pair target can be expressed as

\[
L_N(s):=N^{-2}\sum_{m\ge1}e^{-2sm/N}|p_m|^2
 \longrightarrow \frac{1-e^{-2s}}{4s^2},\qquad s>0.
\]

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/supplement/fixed_map/weighted-secular/determinant_boundary.md}{determinant-ratio reduction}
proves equivalence with all compact weighted pair tests, with an explicit
positive-definite tail bound. No estimate establishing this limit for the
displayed \(U_N\) has been obtained. All-order universality needs more than
this pair target.

\hypertarget{an-exact-adjoint-resolvent-form-of-the-pair-target}{%
\subsection{An exact adjoint-resolvent form of the pair target}\label{an-exact-adjoint-resolvent-form-of-the-pair-target}}

\textbf{Claim ID:} \texttt{BGS-RES-006}. This identity is finite-dimensional and holds
for every unitary \(N\times N\) matrix, not just the frozen family. On the
Hilbert--Schmidt space \(M_N(\mathbb C)\) define

\[
\mathcal U_N(X)=U_N XU_N^*,\qquad
\mathcal D_N=\frac{N^2}{4}\left(2I-\mathcal U_N-\mathcal U_N^*\right),\qquad
T_N(s)=\frac1N\operatorname{Tr}_{HS}(\mathcal D_N+s^2I)^{-1}.
\]

The map \(\mathcal U_N\) is unitary on Hilbert--Schmidt space, so
\(\mathcal D_N\ge0\). If \(e^{i\theta_j}\) are the eigenvalues of \(U_N\), the
matrix units in its eigenbasis diagonalize \(\mathcal D_N\), with eigenvalues
\(N^2\sin^2((\theta_j-\theta_k)/2)\). Summing the Poisson series with
\(q=e^{-2s/N}\) gives the exact identity

\[
1+2L_N(s)=N\sinh(s/N)\cosh(s/N)\,T_N\!\left(N\sinh(s/N)\right).
\]

For every unitary spectrum and every \(s>0\) one also has the uniform comparison

\[
0\le \frac{1+2L_N(s)}{s}-T_N(s)
\le \frac{2}{3N}\cosh(2s/N).                         \tag{R1}
\]

To see the sign and the error, set \(a=s/N\) and
\(y_{jk}=N^2\sin^2((\theta_j-\theta_k)/2)\). The ratio of the \((j,k)\) summand
in \((1+2L_N(s))/s\) to its summand in \(T_N(s)\) is

\[
\frac{\sinh(2a)}{2a}\,\frac{y_{jk}+s^2}{y_{jk}+N^2\sinh^2a}.
\]

It lies between \(1\) and \(\sinh(2a)/(2a)\). Also
\(T_N(s)\le N/s^2\), and
\(\sinh x/x-1\le x^2\cosh(x)/6\) for \(x\ge0\), which proves (R1).
Consequently, for each fixed \(s>0\),

\[
L_N(s)\longrightarrow\frac{1-e^{-2s}}{4s^2}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
T_N(s)\longrightarrow\frac1s+\frac{1-e^{-2s}}{2s^3}.
\]

This is a reformulation of the same open pair limit. It gives no estimate
for \(T_N(s)\) for the prescribed \(U_N\) and no higher-order joint-trace
comparison. The detailed audit and the companion exact
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_spectral_flow_controls.md}{spectral-flow and control identities}
also rule out collapsing the actual iterated kicks into an unordered single
exponential; they do not estimate the ordered product at \(m\asymp N\).

\hypertarget{a-universal-finite-dimensional-abel-floor}{%
\subsection{A universal finite-dimensional Abel floor}\label{a-universal-finite-dimensional-abel-floor}}

\textbf{Claim ID:} \texttt{BGS-TRACE-007}. Every \(N\)-point unitary spectrum satisfies

\[
L_N(s)\ge \frac1{e^{2s}-1},\qquad s>0,                 \tag{R2}
\]

and the bound is attained by a rotated regular \(N\)-gon. Here is the precise
energy reduction. For \(N=1\) the bound is equality directly. For \(N\ge2\), put
\(z_j=e^{i\theta_j}\) and

\[
f_q(r)=\frac{1-q^2}{(1-q)^2+qr},\qquad 0<q<1.
\]

This is strictly completely monotone on \([0,4]\). The regular \(N\)-gon is a
sharp configuration on \(S^1\): it is a circular \((N-1)\)-design and has
\(\lfloor N/2\rfloor\) distinct inner products between different vertices.
Cohn--Kumar, Theorem 1.2 in
\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0607446v2}{\emph{Universally optimal distribution of points on spheres}},
therefore minimizes \(\sum_{j\ne k}f_q(|z_j-z_k|^2)\). The diagonal terms of
the full ordered sum are configuration-independent. If eigenangles
coincide, perturb them to distinct angles and pass to the limit; \(f_q\) is
continuous at zero. Since

\[
\frac{1-q^2}{|1-qe^{it}|^2}
=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^{|m|}e^{imt},
\]

the minimized full sum is \(N^2+2\sum_{m\ge1}q^m|p_m|^2\). For the regular
polygon \(p_m=N\) exactly when \(N\mid m\), and is zero otherwise. Taking
\(q=e^{-2s/N}\) yields (R2).

The CUE benchmark is strictly above this floor:

\[
\frac{1-e^{-2s}}{4s^2}-\frac1{e^{2s}-1}
=\frac{e^{-s}(\sinh^2s-s^2)}{2s^2\sinh s}>0.
\]

Thus (R2) is a sharp universal lower bound but does not identify the frozen
model's limit or give a uniform excess over the clock value.

\hypertarget{smooth-resolvent-transfer-for-the-seven-cut-full-propagator}{%
\subsection{\texorpdfstring{Smooth resolvent transfer for the seven-cut \emph{full} propagator}{Smooth resolvent transfer for the seven-cut full propagator}}\label{smooth-resolvent-transfer-for-the-seven-cut-full-propagator}}

\textbf{Claim ID:} \texttt{BGS-RES-007}. Let \(U_N\) and \(V_N\) be the original and
seven-cut \textbf{full} propagators of \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_seven_cut_reduction.md}{\texttt{BGS-FM-007}}.
For an arbitrary unitary \(W\) write \(L_{W,N}\) and \(T_{W,N}\) for the pair
Abel and adjoint-resolvent functions above. For every compact
\(K\subset(0,\infty)\) and every integer \(r\ge0\), there are constants
\(C_{K,r},N_{K,r}\) such that, for odd \(N\ge N_{K,r}\),

\[
\sup_{s\in K}|\partial_s^r(L_{U,N}(s)-L_{V,N}(s))|
 \le C_{K,r}\frac{\tau}{\log N},                         \tag{R3}
\]

\[
\sup_{s\in K}|\partial_s^r(T_{U,N}(s)-T_{V,N}(s))|
 \le C_{K,r}\left(\frac{\tau}{\log N}+\frac1N\right). \tag{R4}
\]

Thus \(T_{U,N}-T_{V,N}\to0\) in \(C^\infty_{\rm loc}(0,\infty)\).
This is equivalence of any possible scalar-resolvent limits, not
convergence of either resolvent to the CUE value.

\textbf{Proof.} Formula (13) of \texttt{BGS-FM-007} expresses \(L_{W,N}\) as
\(\frac12 C_{2,N}^W(h_s)\) plus terms independent of \(W\), where
\(h_s(x)=s/(s^2+\pi^2x^2)\). All Abel series and their fixed-order
\(s\) derivatives converge absolutely on \(K\) at each \(N\). For every \(r\),
the derivatives \(\partial_s^r h_s\) and their \(x\) derivatives have
uniformly summable unit-interval suprema as \(s\) runs over \(K\);
the \(x\) derivative is \(O_{K,r}(|x|^{-3})\) at infinity. Apply the
phase-coupling estimate (7) there to these differentiated tests.
Its coupled total displacement is \(O(\tau)\), and the seven-cut
occupancy is \(O(N/\log N)\). The spectrum-independent terms cancel,
giving (R3) uniformly on \(K\).

It remains to pass from the Abel functions to the resolvents \textbf{with
derivatives}, since (R1) alone bounds only their values. Set
\(y_{jk}=N^2\sin^2((\theta_j-\theta_k)/2)\),
\(c_N(s)=\sinh(2s/N)/(2s/N)\), and
\(b_N(s)=N^2\sinh^2(s/N)\). The exact identity preceding (R1) gives

\[
R_{W,N}(s):=\frac{1+2L_{W,N}(s)}s-T_{W,N}(s)
=\frac1N\sum_{j,k=1}^N\left[
 \frac{c_N(s)}{y_{jk}+b_N(s)}-\frac1{y_{jk}+s^2}\right]. \tag{R5}
\]

On a fixed small complex neighborhood of \(K\) in \(\Re s>0\) and for all
sufficiently large \(N\), the expansions
\(c_N(s)=1+O_K(N^{-2})\) and \(b_N(s)=s^2+O_K(N^{-2})\)
hold uniformly. Both denominators have modulus at least
\(c_K(1+y_{jk})\) there. Hence each bracket in (R5) is bounded by
\(C_KN^{-2}/(1+y_{jk})\). The \(N^2\) terms and the exterior \(1/N\)
give \(\sup |R_{W,N}|\le C_K/N\) uniformly over \textbf{every} unitary \(W\).
Cauchy's derivative estimates on a slightly smaller neighborhood yield
\(\sup_{s\in K}|\partial_s^rR_{W,N}(s)|\le C_{K,r}/N\).
Subtract (R5) for \(U_N,V_N\) and use (R3), together with the bounded
derivatives of \(1/s\) on \(K\), to obtain (R4). \(\square\)

The proof exploits the already established full-propagator phase coupling;
it neither decomposes \(V_N\) into independent spectra nor evaluates
its scalar resolvent at Heisenberg times. The all-order mixed-resolvent
obligation \texttt{BGS-TRACE-005} therefore remains open. The separate
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/two_clock_gram_falsifier.md}{\texttt{BGS-TRACE-008} two-clock example}
also proves that the necessary Gram moment \(4/3\), simple phases,
macroscopic Haar convergence, uniformly bounded unfolded unit occupancy
and nonvanishing traces cannot replace that obligation.

\hypertarget{what-the-recovered-work-establishes}{%
\subsection{What the recovered work establishes}\label{what-the-recovered-work-establishes}}

For the actual frozen kick, the \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_kick_rank_boundary.md}{exact Jacobi-chain decomposition}
has \(\gcd(N,7)\) irreducible blocks for every odd dimension. With the cited
Hermite--Lindemann input, it implies
\(\operatorname{rank}(U_N-zM_N)\ge N-\gcd(N,7)\) for every complex \(z\) and
every nonzero algebraic coupling. Its approximate-rank bound applies only
before eigenphase wrapping, \(|\tau N|(79/50)\le\pi\); it supplies no fixed-strength
asymptotic control. Separately, the \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_full_lag_resonance.md}{full-lag classical gap}
proves a uniform translated Riesz bound for the exact physical symbol under
the \emph{linear} cat map, including small weighted-Fourier perturbations. It
does not treat transport by the nonlinear kicked map. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/nonlinear_bracket_pressure.md}{nonlinear bracket pressure theorem} shows
that this same \(\lambda^{-r}\) normalization cannot have a uniform upper
bound for the \textbf{actual} nonlinear map: its individual bracket norms grow
at a strictly larger exponential rate. This result is classical and uses
thermodynamic-formalism inputs; none of these results bounds the
Heisenberg-scale joint traces needed for \texttt{BGS-TRACE-005}.

An \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_seven_cut_reduction.md}{exact seven-cut reduction} now gives
\(\|U_N-e^{i\tau N A_N^{\rm cut}}M_N\|_1\le28\pi^2\tau/(25N)\)
for the same fixed coupling. The two \textbf{full} propagators have equivalent
fixed-order sine-kernel targets. Their pair and full Abel statistics differ
by \(O_s(\tau/\log N)\) without assuming a CUE limit. The seven paths
belong only to the generator: every proper union of paths exchanges
Hilbert--Schmidt mass \(d(N-d)/N\) with its complement under the full
propagator. Thus \texttt{BGS-TRACE-005} can be attacked for either full
propagator, with no claim of independent seven-block spectra. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_algebraic_spectral_simplicity.md}{all-minor and simple-spectrum theorem}
removes exact level multiplicity when \(7\nmid N\), while the
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_common_antireversor_certificate.md}{integer commutator-cube certificate}
excludes a common antiunitary reversal of \((A_N,M_N)\) except at \(N=7\).
These results are qualitative and do not estimate near-degenerate spacings.
The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_arithmetic_trace_rigidity.md}{arithmetic trace identity and rigidity theorem}
also proves exact nonvanishing of every \(\operatorname{Tr}U_N^m\)
on the odd sequence and classifies scalar powers. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_effective_gap_floor.md}{effective gap floor} makes spectral
simplicity quantitative for \(7\nmid N\), but its bound is far below
the mean spacing \(N^{-1}\). Neither result supplies an upper bound for
Heisenberg-time traces or the open Abel limit.

Exact algebraic arguments exclude scalar-algebraic returns for the stated
frozen family except its explicitly treated raw \(N=7\) exception. They do not
give microscopic eigenvalue separation. The new qualitative simplicity
theorem covers all odd \(7\nmid N\), whereas the older \emph{quantitative}
finite-size certificates cover only specified dimensions. Structured ergodic comparison
controls unfolded RMS motion of subprincipal perturbations under its stated
Egorov and ergodicity hypotheses; transferring factorial correlations also
needs local occupation moments.

The block-memory analysis distinguishes closed quantum propagation from
reset evolution. Mixing of the positive reset chain does not imply decay
of coherent quantum memory. Actual weighted principal-minor computations
show cancellation within and across frequency windows. They do not justify
independent-phase substitution. A rotated deleted clock has exactly the
CUE characteristic-polynomial covariance and nevertheless regular spacings;
covariance alone therefore does not determine pair statistics.

Full statements, assumptions and proofs are in the topic-indexed supplement.
The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/shadow_tube_history_bridge.md}{shadow-tube analysis}, recovered from the
remote branch, likewise keeps its geometric equidistribution assumption
separate from its proved symbolic filling bound. Both local and remote
research lines are retained.

\hypertarget{a-conditional-route-to-every-compact-correlation-order}{%
\subsection{A conditional route to every compact correlation order}\label{a-conditional-route-to-every-compact-correlation-order}}

For eigenangles \(\theta_j\) in radians and a uniform common origin
\(\alpha\in[0,2\pi)\), put

\[
s_N(w)=\frac1N\sum_j\cot\left(\frac{\theta_j-\alpha}{2}-\frac wN\right).
\]

This Herglotz function has unit-mass particles at
\(N(\theta_j-\alpha)/2+\pi N\ell\), and intensity \(1/\pi\).
Define, using holomorphic extension at coincident arguments,

\[
\begin{split}
\mathcal E_{p,N}(\mathbf w)={}&
\mathbb E[(s_N(w_1)^2+1)\prod_{j=2}^p s_N(w_j)]\\
&+\sum_{j=2}^p\mathbb E\left[
\partial_{w_j}\frac{s_N(w_1)-s_N(w_j)}{w_1-w_j}
\prod_{\ell=2,\ell\ne j}^p s_N(w_\ell)\right].
\end{split}
\]

Theorem 1.9 of Bourgade--Huang,
\href{https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.07617v2}{\emph{Loop Equations Characterize Random Matrix Statistics}, arXiv:2607.07617v2},
provides the external convergence theorem. Our sufficient model hypothesis is

\[
\sup_{\mathbf w\in K^p}
\frac{|\mathcal E_{p,N}(\mathbf w)|}
 {1+\mathbb E\max_j|s_N(w_j)|^{p+1}}\longrightarrow0
\]

for every fixed \(p\) and every compact \(K\subset\mathbb C\setminus\mathbb R\).
The event in that theorem is the whole origin probability space. Its moment
bootstrap then bounds all local particle-count moments, since
\(\mu_N([-B,B])\le(1+B^2)|s_N(i)|\). Uniform integrability upgrades weak
point-process convergence to all compact factorial correlation tests.
Dividing positions by \(\pi\) and integrating the origin gives exactly the
usual deterministic anchored statistic, with normalization \(1/N\).
The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/supplement/fixed_map/resolvent-flow/loop_bridge.md}{detailed bridge}
checks these steps. This is a conditional implication; the model hypothesis
is unproved. It does not assert pointwise correlation densities.

\hypertarget{the-first-two-mixed-equations}{%
\subsection{The first two mixed equations}\label{the-first-two-mixed-equations}}

For arguments in the same half-plane every loop residual vanishes for
every unitary spectrum. Indeed, the nonconstant Fourier frequencies in the
uniform origin all have the same strict sign. Such tests cannot verify
universality.

Fix \(s>0\), \(w=is/2\), \(v=-is/2\), \(q=e^{-2s/N}\), and define

\[
C_N=N^{-3}\sum_{a,b\ge1}q^{a+b}p_{-a}p_{-b}p_{a+b}.
\]

Absolute Fourier convergence gives the exact mixed identity

\[
\mathcal E_{2,N}(w,v)=8i\left(L_N+C_N-\frac1{4s^2}\right).
\]

The cubic quantity \(C_N\) need not be real. Finite circular CUE satisfies
\(\mathbb E(L_N+C_N)=1/(4N^2\sinh^2(s/N))\), so the limiting straight-line
equation has a finite-size correction even in the reference ensemble.

Put \(Z=s_N(w)\), \(M_r=\mathbb E|Z|^r\),
\(e_2=L_N+\Re C_N-1/(4s^2)\), and \(e_3=\mathcal E_{3,N}(w,v,v)\).
Then

\[
e_3=M_4-1-\frac2{s^2}(M_2+1)\in\mathbb R.
\]

To prove this, write \(T=s_N(v)=\bar Z\). Same-half-plane identities give
\(\mathbb ET^2=-1\) and \(\mathbb E(T'T)=0\). Each differentiated quotient,
multiplied by \(T\), has expectation \(-(M_2+1)/s^2\). There are two such
terms; the leading expectation is \(M_4-1\).

For \(P=(Z/i-1)/2\) and \(Q=\mathbb E|P|^4\), Fourier orthogonality yields
\(M_2=1+4L_N\) and \(M_4=1+16L_N+32\Re C_N+16Q\). Eliminating \(C_N\) gives

\[
Q=\left(1+\frac1{2s^2}\right)L_N-\frac1{4s^2}
       +\frac{e_3}{16}-2e_2.
\]

Consequently \(Q\ge L_N^2\) implies

\[
L_N^2-\left(1+\frac1{2s^2}\right)L_N+\frac1{4s^2}
 \le\frac{e_3}{16}-2e_2.
\]

These conclusions require no probabilistic independence. If
\(|e_3|\le\delta_N(1+M_4)\) with \(\delta_N\to0\), Jensen gives, for
\(x=M_2\) and \(t=s^{-2}\),

\[
(1-\delta_N)x^2-2tx-(1+\delta_N+2t)\le0.
\]

Thus \(M_2,M_4\) are bounded and \(e_3\to0\). A normalized vanishing \(p=2\)
residual now also vanishes without normalization. Every subsequential
limit \(\ell\) of \(L_N(s)\) lies in

\[
\frac12+\frac1{4s^2}-\frac12\sqrt{1+\frac1{4s^4}}
 \le\ell\le\frac1{2s^2}.
\]

The interval has positive width. These low-order bounds do not identify
the CUE value or prove convergence; no realizable non-CUE process satisfying
the two vanishing residuals is asserted either. Establishing those residual
hypotheses for the actual map remains a dynamical problem.

\hypertarget{why-a-direct-noise-replacement-does-not-close-the-estimate}{%
\subsection{Why a direct noise replacement does not close the estimate}\label{why-a-direct-noise-replacement-does-not-close-the-estimate}}

There is also an exact identity for depolarizing noise. Let
\(\mathcal P_N(X)=\operatorname{Tr}(X)I/N\) and
\(\Phi_{\eta,N}=e^{-\eta}\mathcal U_N+(1-e^{-\eta})\mathcal P_N\) for
\(\eta\ge0\). The scalar matrices have eigenvalue \(1\) under \(\Phi_{\eta,N}\);
on traceless matrices it acts as \(e^{-\eta}\mathcal U_N\). Therefore

\[
\operatorname{Tr}_{HS}\Phi_{\eta,N}^m
=1+e^{-m\eta}(|p_m|^2-1).
\]

For
\(L_{\eta,N}(s)=N^{-2}\sum_{m\ge1}e^{-2sm/N}\operatorname{Tr}_{HS}\Phi_{\eta,N}^m\),
this gives

\[
L_{\eta,N}(s)=L_N(s+N\eta/2)+\rho_N(s,\eta),\qquad
\rho_N(s,\eta)=\frac1{N^2}\sum_{m\ge1}e^{-2sm/N}(1-e^{-m\eta}),
\]

with \(0\le\rho_N(s,\eta)\le(2Ns)^{-1}\). Noise shifts the unknown
parameter from \(s\) to \(s+N\eta/2\); this identity alone does not recover the
fixed-\(s\) pair limit or control Heisenberg-time traces.

For the unitary Brownian generator \(G=(2N)^{-1}\sum_a D_{H_a}^2\), with
\(\operatorname{Tr}(H_aH_b)=\delta_{ab}\), matrix completeness gives

\[
G|p_m|^2=m^2-m|p_m|^2-
 \frac mN\Re\left(\bar p_m\sum_{a=1}^{m-1}p_a p_{m-a}\right).
\]

Hence exactly

\[
\frac1N GL_N(s)=\frac12\partial_s
 \left[L_N(s)+\Re C_N(s)-\frac{q}{N^2(1-q)^2}\right].
\]

The unknown mixed defect reappears in the attempt to remove noise. For an
exact clock it is nonzero. Moreover, transport directions \(V^jAV^{-j}\)
have identical diagonal entries in a simple eigenbasis of \(V\); Gaussian
linear combinations therefore give rank at most one for instantaneous
eigenphase covariance. Nonlinear bracket effects are not excluded.

A separate elementary obstruction concerns global entropy. On the unfolded
circle of length \(N\), let \(d_N\) be RMS matching distance to a deterministic
configuration, minimized over permutations and common rotation. Labeled
CUE density is at most \(1/N!\) by Hadamard's inequality. A rotation mesh
and a union of Euclidean balls therefore give

\[
Q_N(d_N\le\delta)\le
 \min\left\{1,\left\lceil\frac N\delta\right\rceil
                   (\sqrt{8\pi e}\,\delta)^N\right\}.
\]

Binary relative-entropy contraction shows that \(d_N\to0\) in \(P_N\)
probability forces \(D(P_N\Vert Q_N)/N\to\infty\). Thus global entropy
\(o(N)\) and microscopic RMS preservation cannot both justify the proposed
comparison. This does not exclude local entropy methods or universality.
The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/supplement/fixed_map/resolvent-flow/entropy_obstruction.md}{full proof}
includes the torus-volume and labeling factors.

\hypertarget{the-singular-reference-boundary-and-a-coboundary-control}{%
\subsection{The singular reference boundary and a coboundary control}\label{the-singular-reference-boundary-and-a-coboundary-control}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/cue_singular_energy.md}{Haar-CUE reference proof} (BGS-CUE-001)
evaluates an unregularized object beyond the fixed-positive-\(s\)
pair Abel statistic: if \(F_{N,2}=\sum_{j\ne k} |e^{i\theta_j}-e^{i\theta_k}|^{-2}\), then
\(\mathbb EF_{N,2}=N(N^2-1)/6\) while its variance
is infinite. Centered \(N^{-8/3}F_{N,2}\) has a
spectrally positive \(3/2\)-stable law, derived from the
published Haar-CUE small-gap Poisson limit and a
project determinantal tail bound. The same proof covers
inverse chord powers \(3/2<p<3\).
Moving one eigenphase by \(O(N^{-1})\) can preserve
weak local process limits while making the normalized
unregularized inverse-gap energy diverge. Therefore
neither a weak local limit nor the exact positive-\(s\)
adjoint-resolvent identity permits taking the singular
boundary without an additional gap/uniform-integrability
estimate. None has been established for the maintained
fixed propagator.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/coboundary_spectral_flow_bound.md}{finite coboundary spectral-flow theorem}
(BGS-FLOW-001) controls RMS unfolded phase motion by an
adjoint Birkhoff average of \(H=iN[G,UGU^*]\), with
explicit higher-order commutator errors and a sharp
abstract clock example. Its needed logarithmic-time
average and nested-commutator bounds remain unproved
for the frozen family. The related infinitesimal
calculation (BGS-FLOW-002) shows that Gaussian
coboundary kicks produce a sine drift and no radial
Dyson diffusion. The second-order three-exponential
normal form itself was previously proved in
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/pell_coboundary_resonance.md}{the Pell coboundary note}.
These observations leave the mixed Heisenberg-time
trace obligation unchanged.

\hypertarget{audited-periodic-point-control-from-the-27-september-upload}{%
\subsection{Audited periodic-point control from the 27 September upload}\label{audited-periodic-point-control-from-the-27-september-upload}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_periodic_point_annihilator.md}{all-time annihilator theorem}
(\texttt{BGS-FM-012}) writes
\(C^m=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}x_m&2y_m\\y_m&x_m\end{smallmatrix}\right)\)
for \(C=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)\),
\(C^2=S\), and proves

\[
(S^m-I)^T\mathbb Z^2=
\begin{cases}2x_m\mathbb Z^2,&m\text{ odd},\\
2y_m\mathbb Z\times4y_m\mathbb Z,&m\text{ even}.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus the physical ordinary symbol averages exactly \(-1/10,-1/20,0\)
over the linear-cat fixed-point sets at times \(1,2,\ge3\). This unweighted
identity does not estimate an oscillatory Birkhoff sum or quantum trace.
The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/cue_upload_review_20260927.md}{submission audit} rejects
the proposed upgrade from pair-only TG-mean estimates to all-order CUE.
It also corrects the submitted ordinary-symbol translation, bispectrum
Fourier sign, distinct-index convention and Abel cutoff accuracy.
These controls do not change the Heisenberg-scale joint-trace obligation.

\hypertarget{quadratic-noise-and-its-deterministic-transfer-boundary}{%
\subsection{Quadratic noise and its deterministic-transfer boundary}\label{quadratic-noise-and-its-deterministic-transfer-boundary}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/quadratic_coboundary_noise.md}{quadratic-noise theorem}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-003}) goes beyond the second-order radial obstruction. For
normalized GUE \(G\), put \(X=i[G,UGU^*]/\sqrt2-\mathbb E(i[G,UGU^*]/\sqrt2)\)
and \(m_2=\operatorname{Tr}U^2/N\). Its exact covariance obeys

\[
\frac{1-|m_2|}{N}\operatorname{Tr}T^2
\le\mathbb E(\operatorname{Tr}XT)^2
\le\frac{2+|m_2|}{N}\operatorname{Tr}T^2
\]

for every traceless Hermitian \(T\). It is nonsingular precisely when the
spectrum is not contained in two antipodal points. Inverting the square
root of its covariance yields the infinitesimal traceless Dyson generator.
The raw noise is different: for \(N\ge4\),
\(\int\mathcal L_X|\operatorname{Tr}U^2|^2\,d\mathrm{Haar}=4+2/N^2\).

For a compactly supported smooth local pair statistic, microscopic-time
generators differ by at most
\(C_{R,\phi}|m_2|M^2(1+\log N)+2N^{-2}\sup|x^2\phi''|\)
if every mean-spacing arc contains at most \(M\) phases. That occupancy
bound and its propagation are not proved for the frozen map. A quadratic
noise built from \(d\) Gaussian directions has covariance rank at most
\(d(d+1)/2\); finitely many smooth directions and logarithmically many
frozen-frame time translates do not yield full instantaneous radial rank.
None of these results supplies deterministic noise removal or the required
all-order Heisenberg trace comparison.

\hypertarget{quantitative-quadratic-noise-dynamics-a-scoped-continuation}{%
\subsection{Quantitative quadratic-noise dynamics: a scoped continuation}\label{quantitative-quadratic-noise-dynamics-a-scoped-continuation}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/quadratic_noise_coupling.md}{coupling theorem} (\texttt{BGS-FLOW-004})
compares the raw diffusion \(U_t\) with traceless unitary Brownian motion
\(V_t\) from the same matrix. For \(0\le t\le1\),

\[
N\mathbb E\|U_t-V_t\|_{\rm HS}^2
\le10e^3t(1+|\operatorname{Tr}U_0|^2+|\operatorname{Tr}U_0^2|^2).
\]

Symmetry of the covariance square root cancels the relative Itô
commutator. Every-even-moment estimates strengthen this to
\(N\|U_{t_N}-V_{t_N}\|_{\rm op}\to0\) in probability when the initial
first two traces are bounded and \(t_N\log N\to0\). A separate integrated
translation estimate gives phase-averaged local Laplace and finite-count
comparison for every \(t_N\to0\) with bounded initial low traces, without
an occupancy assumption. Those earlier weak-law estimates alone do not give
unbounded moments; FLOW-016 supplies a separate high-moment transport below.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/quadratic_noise_reversibility.md}{reversible correction}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-005}) is the commuting traceless Hermitian drift

\[
A=-\operatorname{Im}[(m_2+m_1^2/2)U^{*2}+(m_2\bar m_1/2)U^*],
\qquad m_j=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}U^j.
\]

Adding \(D_A\) puts the generator in Haar divergence form. Moreover
\(A=-(4N)^{-1}\operatorname{grad}(|p_2|^2+N^{-1}\operatorname{Re}(p_2\bar p_1^2))\).
For \(N\ge4K\), initial \(|p_1|,|p_2|\le K/2\), and \(t\le1/12\),
Girsanov and an explicit exit estimate give

\[
d_{\rm TV}(P_X^{[0,t]},P_R^{[0,t]})
\le\min(1,2K\sqrt t+16e^{-K^2/(768t)}).
\]

This compares full path laws with the same covariance, not path laws
with Dyson covariance. Haar reversibility does not imply ergodicity;
scalar matrices are absorbing.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/quadratic_noise_trace_fluctuations.md}{fixed-trace theorem}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-006}) assumes every fixed initial trace is uniformly bounded
and the selected initial traces converge. For fixed \(K,T\), it proves
joint path convergence to independent circular complex OU processes
with variance coefficient \(b_k^2=k^2(1+\mathbf1_{k=2}/2)\) and rates

\[
a_X(k)=k/2-\mathbf1_{k=2}/2,\qquad
a_R(k)=k/2+\mathbf1_{k=2}/2.
\]

Uniform maximal trace moments justify the limit. From zero initial
traces the raw second-trace variance is \(6(1-e^{-t})\), whereas Dyson
has \(2(1-e^{-2t})\). Their difference prohibits microscopic operator
coupling at fixed positive time. The reversible limit has variance
\(2(1-e^{-3t})\), with Haar-compatible stationary value two; no finite-\(N\)
stationary convergence or growing-order theorem is implied.

For the odd clock start, the \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/quadratic_noise_clock_limit.md}{local-limit theorem}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-007}) uses the established circular Dyson clock kernel of
Forrester, with a rederived odd-\(N\) normalization and explicit alias
bound. Both quadratic diffusions converge after phase averaging to
Sine\(_2\) at \(t_N\to0\), \(Nt_N\to\infty\), with Laplace error
\(O_f(\sqrt t+(Nt)^{-1}+N^{-2})\). The initial clock has exactly one point
per unit interval while Sine\(_2\) has a positive hole probability.
Thus low traces and bounded occupancy cannot justify generic noise removal.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/fixed_time_wavepacket_trace_bound.md}{direct fixed-time model input}
(\texttt{BGS-FM-013}) is now \textbf{proved at project/author-review level}: every fixed
nonzero power trace is O\_j(1), along all sufficiently large odd N.
Its exact Gaussian frame and sampled packet residual are separate from
Faure's even-dimensional torus formula. The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/quadratic_noise_fixed_time_input.md}{historical source route},
and its sharper action-phase amplitudes remain conditional. The direct
Gaussian overlap bound now gives limsup values below 4 and 9 for the first
two traces, closing K=20 for sufficiently large odd N.
No effective threshold, uniform Heisenberg estimate or all-N initial trace
convergence follows. These results leave \texttt{BGS-TRACE-005} and \texttt{BGS-BGS-001}
open. The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/expansion_wavepacket_review_20261004.md}{current audit}
records the strengthened input and its proof boundary.

\hypertarget{from-finite-coboundary-kicks-to-a-spectral-diffusion}{%
\subsection{From finite coboundary kicks to a spectral diffusion}\label{from-finite-coboundary-kicks-to-a-spectral-diffusion}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/coboundary_fourth_order_drift.md}{fourth-order calculation}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-008}) distinguishes the actual step
\(U\mapsto e^{i\varepsilon(G-UGU^*)}U\) from the raw quadratic diffusion.
In its conjugated logarithm, the expected second-degree Hermitian field
is \(J=-\operatorname{Im}(m_1U^*)\); a further fourth-degree drift remains
even after frozen subtraction of \(J\). Thus covariance alone cannot
identify the limit. Both logarithmic mean terms vanish at \(m_1=0\).

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/coboundary_mobius_diffusion.md}{Möbius reduction}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-009}) uses
\(\Pi(U)=(U-wI)(I-\bar wU)^{-1}\), with the small \(w\) chosen to set
\(\operatorname{Tr}\Pi(U)=0\). The faster field \(J\) lies on common
Möbius orbits. Phase-averaged local Laplace functionals change by
\(O_f(|m_1|)\) under centering, without an occupancy assumption.
At fixed dimension, killed trace moments control the fast mode and
identify the stopped spectral quotient limit at step \(\varepsilon^4/2\)
with generator \(\overline Lf=L_X(f\circ\Pi)\) on the centered slice.
The projected diffusion has an explicit additional Itô drift of operator
norm at most \(80/N^2\) for \(|m_2|\le1/2\); it admits a dimension-uniform
short-time comparison with Dyson motion.

Consequently, for independent normalized GUE kicks and odd clock start,
if \(t_N\to0\) and \(Nt_N\to\infty\),

\[
\lim_{N\to\infty,\ N\ {\rm odd}}\limsup_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}
\left|\mathbb E\Phi_{N,f}
 (U^\varepsilon_{\lfloor2t_N/\varepsilon^4\rfloor})
-\Phi_{\rm Sine}(f)\right|=0.
\]

The chain contains no centering drift or covariance whitening. This proof
first fixes dimension; the following extension supplies an explicit joint
regime. No convergence of the original matrix paths is asserted. The initial clock remains
a counterexample to generic noise removal. This auxiliary theorem does not
establish the deterministic map's Heisenberg joint-trace estimate. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/coboundary_mobius_review_20260929.md}{continuation audit} records
the proof obligations, exact algebra and finite projection checks.

\hypertarget{a-dimension-quantitative-joint-regime-for-the-random-chain}{%
\subsection{A dimension-quantitative joint regime for the random chain}\label{a-dimension-quantitative-joint-regime-for-the-random-chain}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/coboundary_joint_limit.md}{uniform-step theorem} (\texttt{BGS-FLOW-010})
strengthens the fast-coordinate estimate to
\(\mathbb E[|m_1|;j<\sigma]\le C(\varepsilon/N+\varepsilon^4)\).
Its full quartic mean and absolute sixth-order remainder are retained.
Smooth localization gives backward derivative growth \(e^{CNt}\);
a discrete second-trace Lyapunov estimate controls exits directly.
For smooth nonnegative compactly supported tests, the original chain obeys

\[
\left|\mathbb E\Phi_{N,f}
 (U^\varepsilon_{\lfloor2t/\varepsilon^4\rfloor})
-\Phi_{\rm Sine}(f)\right|
\le C_f[\sqrt t+(Nt)^{-1}+N^{-2}+N^{20}e^{CNt}\varepsilon],
\qquad 1/N\le t\le1/12.
\]

Hence \(\varepsilon_N=e^{-N}\), \(t_N\to0\) and \(Nt_N\to\infty\) give
a simultaneous local weak limit. At \(t_N=N^{-2/3}\) the smooth-test rate
is \(O_f(N^{-1/3})\). Nonnegative \(C_c^1\) tests follow by approximation,
without this rate. The displayed exponential step count is not practical.
Its bound also gives a slower polynomial regime at \(t=L_N/N\),
\(L_N\to\infty\), \(L_N=o(\log N)\), \(\varepsilon=N^{-a}\), \(a>20\);
the earlier denial of any polynomial regime is corrected by ERR-026.
No deterministic noise removal follows. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/coboundary_joint_review_20260930.md}{author audit} separates
the analytic proof from exact algebra and finite Frechet-gradient checks.

\hypertarget{polynomial-original-coboundary-steps-with-the-previous-local-rate}{%
\subsection{Polynomial original-coboundary steps with the previous local rate}\label{polynomial-original-coboundary-steps-with-the-previous-local-rate}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/coboundary_polynomial_limit.md}{polynomial continuation}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-011}) proves for the same original chain, odd clock start and
nonnegative \(f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)\) that

\[
\left|\mathbb E\Phi_{N,f}
(U^\varepsilon_{\lfloor2t/\varepsilon^4\rfloor})
-\Phi_{\mathrm{Sine}_2}(f)\right|
\le C_f[\sqrt t+(Nt)^{-1}+N^{-2}
+N^4\varepsilon+tN^9\varepsilon+tN^{10}\varepsilon^2],
\quad 1/N\le t\le1/12.
\]

Here the original kicks retain independent normalized GUE and do not
insert centering or covariance whitening. The proof improves two
dimension estimates. On the localized region \(|m_2|\le3/5\), writing
\(B=N\mathcal C_U\) on the fixed traceless Hermitian Hilbert space,
positive-order derivatives satisfy
\(\|D^rB\|_{\rm op}\le C_r\) and
\(\|D^rB\|_{\rm HS}\le C_r\sqrt N\).
In the differentiated square-root resolvent, placing one derivative in
the latter norm cancels the exterior \(N^{-1/2}\), giving
\(\|D^r\mathcal C_U^{1/2}\|_{\rm HS}\le C_r\).
The rank-two Möbius projection has the same normalized structure.
Its contracted noise drift follows from the exact identities

\[
Q_K=I-\tfrac12(m_2\bar m_1U^*+\bar m_2m_1U),\qquad
Q_L=Q_K+2i(T^*U^*-TU)+2vI-\zeta U^{*2}-\bar\zeta U^2,
\]

where \(T=\sum_a\bar w_aK_a\), \(v=\sum_a|w_a|^2\),
\(\zeta=\sum_aw_a^2\) are the FLOW-009 coefficients.
The derivative norms of drift and noise are dimension-uniform, including
the normalized-trace cutoffs. Stochastic-flow variation estimates yield
\(\|S_sF\|_6\le Ce^{Cs}\|F\|_6\). Retaining the fast coordinate
\(\varepsilon/N+\varepsilon^4\) in the weak sum gives
\(tN^4\|F\|_6(\varepsilon/N+\varepsilon^2)\).

For \(A=\operatorname{Tr}f_{N,\alpha}(U)\ge0\), positivity bounds its first
derivative by \(C_fN\sqrt A\). For orders \(j\ge2\), two direction factors
in Schatten-2 norm bound differentiated Fourier traces by \(C_{f,j}N^j\).
Partition differentiation of \(e^{-A}\) absorbs all remaining powers of
\(A\), proving \(\|\Phi_{N,f}\|_6\le C_fN^6\), even at collisions.
This completes the stated estimate.

Taking \(t=N^{-2/3}\) and \(\varepsilon=N^{-26/3}\) gives exactly
\(2N^{34}\) steps and error \(O_f(N^{-1/3})\). Nonnegative \(C_c^1\) tests
have the weak limit by approximation. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/polynomial_coboundary_review_20261004.md}{review} records the
independent internal check of the new estimates and finite controls.
For a fixed bounded interval \(I\), the local counting generating function
converges to \(\det(I-(1-z)K_I)\) for \(0\le z\le1\); the hole probability
converges to \(\det(I-K_I)\), with \(K_I\) the restricted sine kernel.
Smooth \(L^1\) approximation uses unit intensity; no interval-test rate
or higher-factorial-moment uniform integrability is asserted.
The polynomial exponent is not optimized. FLOW-014 supplies actual-start
relaxation separately at a logarithmic time. Deterministic noise removal
and all-order transfer at that polynomial step schedule remain separate
obligations. FLOW-017 below closes all orders at a different superpolynomial
schedule; deterministic BGS-TRACE-005 and BGS-BGS-001 remain open.

\hypertarget{retaining-the-actual-initial-spectrum-in-the-stochastic-comparison}{%
\subsection{Retaining the actual initial spectrum in the stochastic comparison}\label{retaining-the-actual-initial-spectrum-in-the-stochastic-comparison}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/coboundary_general_start.md}{general-start proof} (\texttt{BGS-FLOW-012})
starts the original uncentered Gaussian coboundary chain at any odd
unitary \(A_N\) with \(|p_1|+|p_2|\le K\). Its normalized traceless Dyson
reference starts at exactly \(\Pi(A_N)\); the algorithm inserts no centering.
For nonnegative compact smooth local Laplace tests, writing
\(n=\lfloor2t/\varepsilon^4\rfloor\) and \(1/N\le t\le1/12\),

\[
\left|\mathbb E\Phi_{N,f}(U_n^\varepsilon)
-\mathbb E\Phi_{N,f}(D_t[\Pi A_N])\right|
\le C_{f,K}[\sqrt t+N^{-1}+N^4\varepsilon+N^9\varepsilon^2
+tN^9\varepsilon+tN^{10}\varepsilon^2].
\]

The fast coordinate has a decaying initial part as well as the stationary
scale \(\rho=\varepsilon/N+\varepsilon^4\). Summation retains
\(h\sum_{j<n}\mathbb E[|m_1(U_j)|;j<\sigma] \le C\varepsilon^2|m_1(A_N)|+Ct\rho\).
The frozen stopped sixth moment bounds exits without an inverse-step
loss from the initial term. The centered initial second trace is \(O_K(1)\),
giving an \(N^{-2}\) initial exit cost. Backward telescoping then adds
\(N^9\varepsilon^2\) to the previous error.
At \(t=N^{-2/3}\), \(\varepsilon=N^{-26/3}\), exactly \(2N^{34}\) steps have
\(O_f(N^{-1/3})\) comparison error. FM-013 supplies \(K=20\) for the actual
frozen map eventually; the Dyson limit at that faster time is still unknown.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/dyson_relaxation_obstruction.md}{prescribed-time obstruction}
(\texttt{BGS-FLOW-013}) constructs, for every selected vanishing \(t_N\), a
schedule-dependent globally uniform simple spectrum with bounded fixed
traces and every positive power trace nonzero. Its Dyson local limit is
empty at that time, both before and after centering. The proof combines
\(\mathbb E N^{-1}\|B_tA-A\|_{\rm HS}^2\le t\) with spectral matching
and \(Q\) narrow balanced clusters. With width \(\delta\) and \(I\subset[-R,R]\),

\[
\mathbb P(X_{N,t}(I)>0)
\le\frac Q\pi(b+2\pi R/N)
+|I|\frac{2\delta^2+(\pi^2/2)t}{b^2}.
\]

Taking \(Q\le\min(N^{1/10},t_N^{-1/6})\) and \(b=Q^{-2}\) proves the
empty limit. Existing EXT-POPESCU-2023 supplies all-power nonvanishing
after one algebraic-exponent perturbation. Under \(Nt_N\to\infty\),
FLOW-012 also transfers the empty limit to the chain at \(\varepsilon=N^{-10}\).
The finite laws retain unit intensity without uniform integrability.
No actual-map counterexample or obstruction to every family-dependent
slower schedule is asserted.

\hypertarget{logarithmic-initial-regularity-and-local-heat-phase-stationary-points}{%
\subsection{Logarithmic initial regularity and local heat-phase stationary points}\label{logarithmic-initial-regularity-and-local-heat-phase-stationary-points}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/frozen_mesoscopic_regularity.md}{corollary} (\texttt{BGS-FM-017}) uses the
existing FM-007 bound \(|p_j(U_N)|\le CN^{39/40}\) for
\(1\le j\le J_N=\lfloor c\log N\rfloor\). For
\(H_A(z)=N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}[(A+z)(A-z)^{-1}]\) and
\(d_N=CN^{-1/40}\), the absolutely convergent trace series gives

\[
\sup_{|z|\le e^{-g}}|H_{U_N}(z)-1|
\le\frac{2[d_N+e^{-(J_N+1)g}]}{1-e^{-g}}.
\]

At \(g_N=4\log J_N/J_N\) this tends to zero. Centering contributes only
\(C/[N(1-e^{-g_N})^2]\), so the exact reference initial spectrum has
uniform Poisson-smoothed density down to that logarithmic scale.
Every fixed angular derivative also converges at the larger scale
\(J_N^{-1/2}\). This is not a microscopic local law.

At \(t_N=\sqrt{g_N}\), FLOW-012 gives vanishing comparison error
\(O_f(g_N^{1/4})+o(1)\) for \(\varepsilon=N^{-10}\).
For the centered eigenangles \(\alpha_j\), the local phase

\[
\mathcal S_N(\zeta;\theta)=\frac{(\zeta-\theta)^2}{2t_N}
+\frac1N\sum_j\log\left[2\sin\frac{\zeta-\alpha_j}{2}\right]
\]

has unique stationary points in the radius-\(t_N/8\) disks about
\(\theta\pm it_N/2\), with shifts \(o(t_N)\) and
\(t_N\mathcal S_N''=1+o(1)\) uniformly in \(\theta\).
A contraction proof uses \(\mathcal S_N'=(\zeta-\theta)/t_N -iH_A(e^{i\zeta})/2\) and Cauchy bounds in the two off-real strips.
The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/circular_kernel_route_20261004.md}{route note} credits the
prior arbitrary-start determinantal formula and checks its normalization.
The real logarithmic potential additionally bounds the unweighted
vertical phase tails by \(C\sqrt{t_N/N}\,e^{N a_N(\theta,t_N/2)-cNt_N}\)
outside the two stationary neighborhoods. This uses positivity of the
initial Herglotz real part near the real axis and the trace-series bound
away from it, with no lower-gap assumption. The full kernel's amplitudes
are not bounded by this estimate alone; the separate FLOW-014 argument
below handles them. Even the whole
logarithmic trace window cannot abstractly select \(t=N^{-2/3}\):
the FLOW-013 family at that time satisfies it and still has an empty limit.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/general_start_review_20261004.md}{review} states the
independent internal proof-checking boundary. Deterministic noise removal
and the original signed Heisenberg hierarchy remain open.

\hypertarget{actual-start-circular-relaxation-and-the-original-chain-sine-law}{%
\subsection{Actual-start circular relaxation and the original-chain Sine law}\label{actual-start-circular-relaxation-and-the-original-chain-sine-law}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/circular_dyson_actual_start.md}{full proof} (\texttt{BGS-FLOW-014}) uses
the prior arbitrary-start circular Brownian biorthogonal kernel of
Kieburg--Li--Zhang--Forrester, with source time \(t/(2N)\) and angular
measure \(d\theta/(2\pi)\). Its sine-product interpolation and backward
Gaussian heat representation give an exact double contour plus a
crossing term. The crossing-pole residue is negative before rearrangement;
the resulting kernel receives the full positive residue, not a half-residue.
All circle windings are retained.

Let \(E_N\) be the initial Herglotz error on the strips \(|\Im z|\ge t/8\),
and \(v_N\) the real-potential error beyond \(g\le t/8\), as explicitly
defined in the full proof. When \(E_N\to0\), \(v_N/t\to0\) and \(Nt\to\infty\),
Cauchy bounds give global horizontal convexity and vertical concavity
of the phase, not merely nonzero local Hessians. The near-axis central
barrier comes from FM-017. With \(w=\sqrt{t/N}\), the remaining pole
amplitude is controlled by

\[
\int_{\mathbb R^2}\frac{e^{-|z-a|^2/(4w^2)}}{|z-c|}\,d^2z\le Cw,
\]

uniformly even when the Gaussian center and pole coincide.
Period-cell summation and the \(N/t\) prefactor then give a remainder
\(C_R\sqrt{N/t}\) in each fixed microscopic window. There are no separately
estimated initial-gap denominators. Define the unfolded kernel by

\[
\widehat K_{N,t}^{\theta_0}(x,y)
=N^{-1}K_{N,t}(\theta_0+2\pi x/N,\theta_0+2\pi y/N).
\]

The explicit crossing term yields, uniformly in \(\theta_0\) and \(|x|,|y|\le R\),

\[
\left|\widehat K_{N,t}^{\theta_0}(x,y)
-\frac{\sin\pi(x-y)}{\pi(x-y)}\right|
\le C_R[E_N+(Nt)^{-1/2}].
\]

Hadamard bounds and determinant telescoping are summable after division
by \(k!\), so the entire Laplace/Fredholm series converges with that error.
Gap-independent estimates pass to repeated initial levels by continuity
of the bounded Laplace test. Full and traceless Brownian motion have
exactly the same uniform-origin observable.

For \(A_N=\Pi U_N\), the actual logarithmic trace input gives the required
errors at \(g_N=4\log J_N/J_N\), \(t_N=8g_N\), and
\(E_N+(Nt_N)^{-1/2}=o(\sqrt{g_N})\). Balanced comparison parameters are

\[
\varepsilon_N=N^{-9}/\sqrt{t_N},\qquad
n_N=\lfloor2t_N^3N^{36}\rfloor.
\]

FLOW-012's six terms reduce to
\(\sqrt t\), \(N^{-1}\), \(N^{-5}/\sqrt t\), \(N^{-9}/t\),
\(\sqrt t\), \(N^{-8}\), all \(O(\sqrt t)\) for \(t\ge1/N\).
Thus the original uncentered chain from the unchanged \(U_N\) has

\[
\mathbb E\Phi_{N,f}(U_{n_N}^{\varepsilon_N})
=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{Sine}_2}(f)+O_f(\sqrt{g_N}),
\qquad 0\le f\in C_c^\infty.
\]

This closes the actual-start stochastic relaxation step at the stated
logarithmic time, with an ineffective startup threshold. It does not
compare the noisy spectrum with its deterministic initial spectrum,
prove relaxation at \(N^{-2/3}\), or transfer unbounded correlations of the
original chain. Deterministic BGS remains open. The new analytic
implications received an independent internal audit; the prior finite
kernel and inherited project proofs retain their separate trust boundaries.
No external referee report, priority or prize-level significance is asserted.

\hypertarget{all-local-moments-and-the-original-chain-signed-criterion}{%
\subsection{All local moments and the original-chain signed criterion}\label{all-local-moments-and-the-original-chain-signed-criterion}}

\textbf{Claim IDs:} \texttt{BGS-FLOW-016}, \texttt{BGS-FLOW-017}. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/local_moment_transport.md}{transport proof} matches two period-N fields
with averaged unfolded displacement cost
\(c_{p,N}=N^{-1}\sum_j|d_j|^p\). Let
\(M(u)=\sup_{r\ge1}B_N([u-r,u+r])/(2r)\) be the reference maximal density.
Its fixed moments are bounded by the periodic Hardy--Littlewood estimate
and the reference's fixed unit-window moments. If
\(n=A_N([u-R,u+R])>16(R+1)M\), matching and packing give

\[
\sum_{a_j+\ell N\in[u-R,u+R]}|d_j|^p
\ge\frac{3n^{p+1}}{4\,16^pM^p}.
\]

Hölder and origin integration bound all target count moments \(1<s<p+1\).
If \(\mathbb Ec_{p,N}\to0\), positive Laplace tests transfer the weak law;
the moment bound supplies uniform integrability for every factorial order
\(k<p+1\). All fixed vanishing transport moments therefore transfer every
fixed factorial order. Collapsing K clock points at one location has cost
\(N^{-1}\sum_{j<K}j^p\) and kth factorial mean \((K)_k/N\). At \(N\sim K^k\)
this refutes extending a single pth cost to \(k>p+1\). No critical-endpoint
or growing-order theorem is asserted.

Along a unitary logarithm path, Jensen for eigenangle speeds and
Schatten triangle give the matching inequality

\[
c_{p,N}(V,W)\le\frac{N^{p-1}}{4^p}\operatorname{Tr}|V-W|^p.
\]

For the projected diffusion Y and its coupled Dyson reference V, stop the
comparison at \(|p_2(Y)|=K_{N,r}\) with
\(K_{N,r}^2=C_{K,r}(1+t\log N)\). The inherited covariance and drift
estimates bound both matrix brackets by
\((4K_{N,r}^2+44)N^{-2}I\,ds\). The Hermitian-dilation moment inequality
and the exponential trace exit tail yield

\[
\mathbb Ec_{2r,N}(Y_t,V_t)
\le C_{K,r}(t+t^2\log N)^r+C_{K,r}N^{-2r-4}\to0.
\]

This holds when \(t\to0\), \(t^2\log N\to0\), including the actual
\(t=8g\) with \(g=4\log J/J\), \(J=\lfloor c\log N\rfloor\).
It proves no largest-displacement estimate at this time. FLOW-014's
gap-independent kernel bounds supply reference count moments, including
repeated starts by fixed-N continuity of bounded smooth factorial majorants.
Thus the projected diffusion has all fixed local factorial limits.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/coboundary_all_order_limit.md}{original-chain proof} strengthens
localization to \(\mathbb P(\sigma\le n)\le C_{L,K}(N^{-L}+N^4\varepsilon)\)
for every fixed L. It uses the frozen stopped fast moments and
\(|p_2|^{2r}\) Lyapunov tests; no inverse-power initial-layer loss occurs.
The exact partition/Fourier formula gives polynomial \(C^6\) derivative
norms for each fixed factorial test without spectral-gap denominators.
The dimension-uniform backward semigroup and fast terminal centering then
transfer every fixed test for one sequence satisfying
\(N^b\varepsilon_N\to0\) for all fixed b. The algorithm remains

\[
U_{j+1}=\exp[i\varepsilon_N(G_j-U_jG_jU_j^*)]U_j,
\qquad U_0=U_N,
\]

with fresh normalized GUE. At the actual logarithmic time one may take
\(\varepsilon_N=N^{-\log\log N}\) and
\(n_N=\lfloor2t_NN^{4\log\log N}\rfloor\).
This schedule is superpolynomial; the earlier polynomial bounded-Laplace
result remains valid with its original scope.

Spatial ergodicity of Sine\(_2\), from Soshnikov's prior Theorem 7, turns
the barycenter limit and moment bounds into one-chain origin-average
convergence in \(L^2\). For a fixed block average \(\mathcal A_S\varphi\),
periodicity and Jensen give

\[
\mathbb E_\omega|F_N(\omega)-c|^2
\le\int|\mathcal A_S\varphi-c|^2dQ_N.
\]

Take \(N\to\infty\) at fixed S using uniform integrability, then
\(S\to\infty\) using the mean ergodic theorem. Schwartz tails also remove
tuples using two copies of the same circle label, whose diameter is at
least N. Hence, writing
\(W_N(m;A)=\sum_\pi\mu(\pi)\prod_{B\in\pi}p_{\sum_{i\in B}m_i}(A)\),
for every fixed \(\widehat\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^k)\),

\[
\mathbb E_\omega\left|
\frac1{N^k}\sum_{\sum_i m_i=0}\widehat\psi(m/N)
\left[W_N(m;U_{n_N})-\mathbb E_{\rm CUE}W_N(m;V_N)\right]
\right|^2\to0.
\]

Every partition counterterm and \(p_0=N\) remains present; the modulus
stays outside the whole signed sum. This is a stochastic theorem.
For the original one-step Markov operator \(T_\varepsilon\), the exact
discrete defect is

\[
\mathfrak D^{\rm chain}_{N,\psi}
=\sum_{j<n_N}\mathbb E[(T_{\varepsilon_N}-I)F_{N,\psi}(U_j)]
=\mathbb EF_{N,\psi}(U_{n_N})-F_{N,\psi}(U_N).
\]

The deterministic complete signed CUE target for each fixed test is now
equivalent to \(\mathfrak D^{\rm chain}_{N,\psi}\to0\), or to
\(\mathbb E|F_{N,\psi}(U_{n_N})-F_{N,\psi}(U_N)|^2\to0\).
Its actual vanishing remains open. Independent internal review checked the
new implications; inherited inputs keep their stated evidence levels.
The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/evidence/executions/20261005/all-order/manifest.json}{finite packet}
and \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/literature/all_order_sources_20261005.md}{source review} do not
establish deterministic noise removal, world priority, external refereeing,
an all-order polynomial schedule, or full BGS.

\hypertarget{the-exact-deterministic-noise-removal-obligation}{%
\subsection{The exact deterministic noise-removal obligation}\label{the-exact-deterministic-noise-removal-obligation}}

\textbf{Claim ID:} \texttt{BGS-FLOW-015}. The
\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/microscopic_noise_removal.md}{full proof} retains the unchanged \(U_N\)
and the positive uniform-origin local Laplace test \(\Phi_{N,f}\).
For normalized unitary Brownian motion, let
\(P_tF(A)=\mathbb E F(B_tA)\) and

\[
G_N=\frac1{2N}\sum_j\partial_j^2+
\frac1{2N}\sum_j\sum_{k\ne j}
\cot\frac{\theta_j-\theta_k}{2}\partial_j.
\]

The generator applied to the smooth Laplace function extends through
collisions by cancellation of its paired derivative differences.
At each fixed dimension, the exact signed identity is

\[
\mathfrak D_{N,f}(A,t)=\int_0^tP_s(G_N\Phi_{N,f})(A)ds
=P_t\Phi_{N,f}(A)-\Phi_{N,f}(A).
\]

FLOW-014 applies directly to the uncentered \(U_N\) using FM-007's
logarithmic trace estimate. Consequently its deterministic weak local
Sine\(_2\) law is equivalent to \(\mathfrak D_{N,f}(U_N,t_N)\to0\)
for every nonnegative \(f\in C_c^\infty\), at the proved logarithmic time
\(t_N=8g_N\). The modulus stays outside the full signed integral.
This equivalence does not establish its vanishing or the stronger
unbounded factorial-moment target TRACE-005.

The full mixed-trace generator splits and merges factor positions,
including the factor \(p_0=N\) on opposite-index merging. It preserves
the finite spaces of charge-zero products with positive degree at most q.
Those spanning symbols need not be independent when \(q\ge N\);
finite closure does not give uniformly bounded complexity or a
fixed-correlation-order closure. The exact inclusion-exclusion/Fourier
formula still involves signed mixed traces with indices of order N.
FM-007's \(e^{Cm}\) error control does not reach that range.

Four precise boundaries follow.

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\item
  For a test supported in width \(w<1\), a spectrum with minimum unfolded
  gap greater than w has \(\Phi_{N,f}=1-a_f\) on an open neighborhood,
  where \(a_f=\int(1-e^{-f})\). Hence every initial generator iterate and
  right heat derivative is zero. Nevertheless the simple family
  \(A_N=\operatorname{diag}(e^{iN^{-4}},e^{2\pi i/N},\ldots, e^{2\pi i(N-1)/N})\) has all positive traces nonzero and the whole
  logarithmic trace window, but whenever \(t_N\to0\), \(Nt_N\to\infty\),

  \[
  \mathfrak D_{N,f}(A_N,t_N)\to\delta_f
  \ge(1-a_f/3)e_2>0,
  \]

  \[
  e_2=\frac12\iint h(x)h(y)
  \left[1-\left(\frac{\sin\pi(x-y)}{\pi(x-y)}\right)^2\right]dxdy,
  \qquad h=1-e^{-f}.
  \]

  The proof uses the prior clock theorem and a uniform-origin
  \(O_f(N^{-3})\) comparison. It refutes the heat-jet transfer shortcut.
  Its strict-gap hypothesis is not established for the actual map.
\item
  At a deterministic matrix put \(X=|p_1|^2\), \(W=X^2\) and
  \(Z=\Re(p_2\bar p_1^2)\). The exact equations
  \(G_NX=1-X\) and \(G_NW=-2W-2Z/N+4X\) give

  \[
  \max\{|G_NX|,|G_NW|\}\ge(\sqrt{17}-1)/4-2K^3/N
  \quad\text{if } |p_1|+|p_2|\le K.
  \]

  FM-013 makes this an eventual actual-map bound with K=20.
  Unscaled full-class stationarity fails; the normalized microscopic
  mixed loop hierarchy remains a possible route.
\item
  The normalized character of highest weight \((r,0,\ldots,0,-r)\)
  has sup norm one and heat multiplier
  \(e^{-tr(r+N-1)/N}\). At \(r=N\), any sup-norm left inverse containing
  this mode has norm at least \(e^{(2N-1)t}\), exceeding every fixed
  polynomial at the chosen logarithmic time. This standard character
  calculation concerns a global growing-degree function space,
  not instability for one fixed local Laplace test.
\item
  The stationary periodic point field of every finite deterministic
  spectrum has infinite relative entropy to Poisson on every interval
  of length at least two, and infinite specific entropy. An adjacent
  gap \(d\le1\) produces an event of a fixed pair distance with positive
  probability \((2-d)/N\), whereas Poisson gives that event probability zero.
  The published Sine-beta free-energy minimizer characterization does
  not supply finite-entropy near-minimality of those raw fields.
  A limit-level or justified regularized variational argument remains open.
\end{enumerate}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/literature/noise_removal_sources_20261005.md}{source audit}
credits the character heat input and entropy definition. A bounded packet
checks 348 independent exact radial/trace identities, 630 charge-closure
cases, literal low-trace rows, finite character and rational gap controls,
and separate quadrature diagnostics. Two internal proof passes checked
the new implications. These controls do not establish the outstanding
model-specific defect estimate, external referee validation or priority.

\hypertarget{prime-resonant-blocks-and-the-actual-sector-obligation}{%
\subsection{Prime-resonant blocks and the actual sector obligation}\label{prime-resonant-blocks-and-the-actual-sector-obligation}}

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/prime_resonant_sector.md}{prime-resonant audit} (\texttt{BGS-TRACE-009})
retains the exact left-to-right block
\[
C_{p,d_p}=\prod_{j=0}^{d_p-1}e^{i\tau p M_p^jA_pM_p^{-j}},\qquad
U_p^{rd_p}=\zeta_p^r C_{p,d_p}^r.
\]
The known order relation \(d_p\mid p-(2/p)\) and the integer determinant
give \(d_p>2\log p/\log(3+2\sqrt2)\). For a compact window
\(K\subset[a,b]\subset(0,\infty)\), let \(S_p(K)\) be the normalized
absolute resonant comparison and \(E_p(K)\) the normalized actual
trace-square mass. Then
\[
|S_p(K)-E_p(K)|\le(b-a)/d_p+1/p.
\]
Thus the whole-sector comparison vanishes exactly when its actual
mass does. A single deterministic trace need not equal its CUE ensemble
expectation. The correct reference block is a Haar power, whose smaller
independent component law is Rains' prior theorem; it is not Haar CUE
of dimension \(p\).

The exact Fejer pullback is an average of microscopic pair kernels
centered at all rational shifts \(h/d_p\). A baseline \(1+o(1)\) for that
comb would dispose of the sector; this quantitative hypothesis remains
unproved for the frozen map. Conversely, a trace of size at least \(cp\)
at positive bounded Heisenberg times on an infinite prime subsequence
would already obstruct the pair law through a positive time-mass.
Finite coherence at \(|\tau|p^2\ll1\) is not such a subsequence.

The selected invariant -98 and candidate prime list were reproduced
exactly. At 29 the selected orbit sum is 903/1000; at 97 the norm-colliding
candidate points lie in another orbit and the sum is 9/10. Neither
prime needs exclusion from the scalar test. The stronger scalar-power
exclusion is prior FM-010 and gives no upper trace bound.
Nonresonant powers, composite dimensions and higher joint correlations
remain outside this reduction. TRACE-005 and BGS-BGS-001 remain open.

\hypertarget{a-universal-boundary-on-the-norm-used-for-the-deterministic-target}{%
\subsection{A universal boundary on the norm used for the deterministic target}\label{a-universal-boundary-on-the-norm-used-for-the-deterministic-target}}

\href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/signed_heisenberg_comparison.md}{TRACE-010} proves that the unaveraged
all-order absolute CUE trace criterion is impossible. If
\(N^{-2}\sum_{j\in[N/8,N/2]}||p_j|^2-j|\to0\), then
\[
\liminf N^{-1/2}N^{-3}\sum_{m,n\in[N/8,N/4]}
|D_N(m,n,-m-n)-2(N-m-n)|\ge1/1024.
\]
The same obstruction grows as \(N^{k/2-1}\) at every fixed \(k\ge3\)
on the stated positive cones. It does not refute BGS: the exact
microscopic bridge uses the weighted \textbf{signed} sum, with a modulus
outside the whole sum. TRACE-003's absolute sufficient implication
remains correct, including averages taken before the modulus; its
simultaneous unaveraged all-order premise is excluded.

The continuation calibrates the signed factorial cubic with an exact
Haar-CUE complex variance for arbitrary low-band weights. Its reference
root mean square scale is \(O(N^{-1/2})\), with variance
\(O(1/(Nd)+1/N^2)\) on the three resonant strips. These are reference
laws, not estimates for this map. A formal quadratic-phase trace table
exhibits rapid signed cancellation but fails moment positivity already
at \(N=3\); it is not a unitary construction.

The next direct model-specific attack is the full signed factorial cubic,
separating \(d_p\mid m\), \(d_p\mid n\), and \(d_p\mid m+n\) with the actual
ordered block and retaining the nonzero CUE counterterms above the ramp.
The pair-sector mass alone loses a factor of order \(\sqrt{N/d}\) in the
available absolute Cauchy--Schwarz estimate. No such signed actual-map
bound is proved. TRACE-005 and BGS-BGS-001 remain open.

\hypertarget{resonant-cubic-deletion-from-local-spectral-density}{%
\subsection{Resonant cubic deletion from local spectral density}\label{resonant-cubic-deletion-from-local-spectral-density}}

\textbf{Claim ID:} \texttt{BGS-TRACE-011}. The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/resonant_cubic_density_control.md}{full proof}
closes a conditional sector question and identifies a sharp tail obstruction.
It gives no unconditional Heisenberg estimate for the frozen map.

For the occupancies \(n_h\) of the \(N\) intervals of length \(1/N\), put
\(M_s=N^{-1}\sum_h n_h^s\). Fix \(0<a<b\), \(2b<1\), positive times in
\([aN,bN]\), and let \(E_N=N^{-2}\sum_{j\in[aN,2bN],d\mid j}|p_j|^2\).
For every compact smooth complex weight W, the signed union of the three
resonant strips satisfies
\[
\left|N^{-3}\sum_{\substack{m,n\in[aN,bN]\\d\mid m\text{ or }d\mid n\text{ or }d\mid(m+n)}}
 W(m/N,n/N)p_mp_n\overline{p_{m+n}}\right|
 \le C_W\sqrt{E_N M_4}.
\]
The modulus is outside the entire sum. More generally, for \(3<s\le4\),
the bound is \(C_{W,s}E_N^{(s-3)/(s-2)}M_s^{1/(s-2)}\).
It has no cardinality loss. With \(Q_N=N^{-2}\sum_{j\in[aN,2bN]}|p_j|^2\)
and \(\ell=|[aN,bN]\cap\mathbb Z|/N\), the factorial counterterms cost at most
\[
\|W\|_\infty\left[3\ell E_N+6(\ell/d+1/N)Q_N
                   +12b\ell(\ell/d+1/N)\right].
\]
Therefore \(d\) tending to infinity, \(E\) tending to zero and bounded \(M_s\) for
some \(s>3\) delete the full resonant factorial cubic. Critical cubic uniform
integrability is an alternative to the higher moment. Bounded \(M_3\) alone fails.

The proof retains phases. A positive Gaussian density at scale 1/N has
Fourier coefficients \(e^{-(m/N)^2}p_m/N\), and its \(L^s\) norm to the \(s\) power
is comparable to \(M_s\). Smooth frequency filters have uniformly integrable
convolution kernels. The projection onto \(d\)-divisible modes is the positive
average over shifts \(h/d\). Parseval supplies its \(L^2\) bound by the square root
of \(E\); Holder supplies \(L^4\) bounds for the other two factors. General \(W\) follows
by Fourier inversion with translation-independent kernel norms. The union
indicator equals the three strip indicators minus twice the common
intersection. Direct incidence counting gives the displayed counterterm
budget, including the \(m+n\) strip.

The critical obstruction is realizable. Take \(N=dq^3\), \(q\) copies of a \(d\)-clock
and an \((N-dq)\)-clock background. Its active traces are
\(dq\,\mathbf1_{d\mid m}\), its \(E\) is \(O(1/q)\), \(M_3\) is bounded and \(M_4\) has order \(q\).
Yet its resonant factorial cubic tends to the integral of \(W\). Tiny phase
perturbations make the spectrum simple and preserve these limits.
The interpolation exponents have constant-order budget on this family.

There is a stronger variant: for odd \(q=2^l+1\), \(d=q\) and \(N=q^4\), select
an \((N-q^2)\)-dimensional CUE background instead. Deterministic simple
realizations exist which satisfy every compact smooth signed CUE pair
comparison and have vanishing resonant mass and bounded \(M_3\), while both
the resonant and full-box factorial cubic tend to the integral of \(W\) for
\(0<a<b<1/4\). All-band pair variance follows from a finite projection
cumulant bound \(|\kappa_4|\le26(N-q^2)\). The second/fourth/sixth mixed
cubic moments use Diaconis--Evans only when \(4bN\le N-q^2\).
Microscopic count covariances are controlled by positive block determinants,
not by independent-bin assumptions. Uniform negative-Sobolev bounds and
summability justify all smooth cubic weights. These are abstract spectra,
not the frozen map, prime-period theorems or weak-process counterexamples.

For the actual primes, the oriented block from TRACE-009 gives exactly
the \(E\) above. The needed block-mass bound and spectral density tails remain
open. The quantitative alternative \(E=O(1/d_p)\) with \(M_4=o(d_p)\) also suffices.
When \(d_p\) is comparable to \(p\), bounded \(Q\) and \(E\) tending to zero already close
the sector by the earlier finite-cardinality budget. The new mechanism
addresses growing sectors without assuming they exhaust the prime orders.
Nonresonant signed cubic cancellation, other cones, composites and every
higher factorial order remain separate obligations. A raw \(k\)-factor version
has budget \(C_{W,k}\sqrt{E_N M_{2(k-1)}}\), but does not automatically treat
proper subset resonances and CUE counterterms. TRACE-005 and BGS-BGS-001
remain open; no change to the coupling, unfolding or symmetry class is made.

\hypertarget{folded-square-refinement-and-block-crowding}{%
\subsection{Folded-square refinement and block crowding}\label{folded-square-refinement-and-block-crowding}}

\textbf{Claim ID:} \texttt{BGS-TRACE-012}. The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/folded_quadratic_resonance_control.md}{proof}
sharpens the preceding sufficient density input. With the same positive
Gaussian density and arithmetic projection, put
\(G_d=\|P_d(\rho_N^2)\|_2^2\). For every smooth compact complex weight,
the signed three-strip cubic satisfies
\[
|Z_N(W)|\le C_W\sqrt{E_NG_d},\qquad
1\le\|\rho_N\|_2^4\le G_d\le\|\rho_N\|_4^4.
\]
The modulus stays outside the full sum. The factorial counterterm budget
from TRACE-011 is unchanged. Since \(Q_N\le e^{8b^2}\sqrt{G_d}\),
\(E_NG_d\to0\) and \((1/d+1/N)\sqrt{G_d}\to0\) suffice for deletion.
For actual prime orders \(d\le N+1\), \(G_d=o(d^2)\) suffices for the
second condition. These actual-map estimates are not proved.

The improvement comes from moving the self-adjoint projection onto
the product of the other two filtered factors. Positivity of the
multiplier-kernel majorants gives
\(\|P_d(F_uF_v)\|_2\le C_{u,v}\|P_d(\rho_N^2)\|_2\).
Projected factors and the common intersection obey the same estimate.
Fourier inversion with modulation-independent kernel norms treats W.
An explicit simple-spectrum separation uses \(N=L^4\), \(d=L^3\), \(K=L^2\):
an \((N-K)\)-clock plus a tiny split cluster gives \(E_NM_4\gtrsim L\),
but \(E_NG_d=O(L^{-2})\) and a vanishing resonant factorial cubic.
This abstract spectrum is not claimed to satisfy CUE pairs or be the map.

Write \(C=U^d\) and \(R=N/d\). For \(C=\zeta^{-1}U^d\), rotate the original
phases by a d-th-root phase of \(\zeta^{-1}\); \(E\), \(Q\) and \(G_d\) are unchanged.
The normalized block density is
\(f_{C,R}(u)=d^{-1}\sum_{j,v}\eta(R(u+dx_j+v))\).
For \(g_h(u)=\rho_N((u+h)/d)\) define
\(B_d=d\sum_hg_h^2/(\sum_hg_h)^2\). Then exactly
\[
P_d\rho_N(x)=f_{C,R}(dx),\qquad
G_d=\int B_d(u)^2 f_{C,R}(u)^4du,\qquad 1\le B_d\le d.
\]
The block spectrum does not determine root allocation \(B_d\).
Concentrated and balanced lifts of the same \(C=I\) give a \(d^2\) energy
ratio when \(N/d\) tends to infinity. Keeping only the block density
therefore loses relevant information. Equivalent positive formulas are
\[
G_d=\frac1d\sum_{h=0}^{d-1}\int\rho_N(x)^2\rho_N(x+h/d)^2dx
=\sum_{r\in\mathbb Z}|\widehat{\rho_N^2}(rd)|^2.
\]
The proof expands the latter as an absolutely convergent fourth
joint-trace energy, providing an explicit dynamical target.

A separate obstruction needs no root-allocation assumption. If K block
phases lie in an arc of turn length \(\varepsilon d/N<1\), the positive
anchored factorial r-point measure satisfies
\[
\mu_{N,r}([-\varepsilon,\varepsilon]^{r-1})
\ge\frac{(d-s)(t)_r+s(t+1)_r}{N}
\ge\frac{(K-(r-1)d)_+^r}{Nd^{r-1}},\quad K=dt+s.
\]
This follows by lifting the arc to d microscopic intervals and
balancing their counts, using discrete convexity of the falling factorial.
When \(d=o(N)\), \(\varepsilon\to0\) and
\(K\ge c(Nd^{r-1})^{1/r}\), this excludes Sine factorial comparison.
The argument uses a fixed smooth positive neighborhood before shrinking
it; no weak-process conclusion is inferred from moment mass alone.

The Sine cubic cube mass, and the finite CUE expectation of that mass,
are at most \((3\pi^6/5)\varepsilon^8\). A probability-frequency Gram
identity, Newton divided differences and Hadamard prove this uniform
nonoptimal bound. The actual \(p=239\), \(d=7\) operator gives a finite
application: \(\|A_p+I/10\|\le26/25\) and telescoping put all \(K=p\) block
phases in the required arc with \(\varepsilon<3\cdot10^{-76}\).
Its factorial cubic mass is at least \(254694/239\), while the finite
CUE expectation is below \(10^{-600}\). This is analytically certified
at the actual coupling; it is finite coherence, not an infinite-prime
BGS obstruction. The balanced count is a minimum, not a computation
of the actual root multiplicities.

The available degree-\(L\) ordered Duhamel remainder is at most
\(H^{L+1}/(L+1)!\), with \(H=(26/25)|\tau|Nm\). At Heisenberg times
\(m\asymp N\), \(H\) grows as \(|\tau|N^2\); a fixed-degree certificate
does not decay. Fixed orbit moments alone do not justify the required
growing word expansion. Nonperturbative E/G estimates, nonresonant
signed cancellation and the complete TRACE-005/BGS-BGS-001 goals
remain open. The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/folded_quadratic_review_20261001.md}{review}
separates proof, finite controls and prior work.

\hypertarget{fixed-time-bounded-traces-and-quantizer-overlap}{%
\subsection{Fixed-time bounded traces and quantizer overlap}\label{fixed-time-bounded-traces-and-quantizer-overlap}}

\textbf{Claim IDs:} \texttt{BGS-FM-013}, \texttt{BGS-FM-016}. The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/fixed_time_wavepacket_trace_bound.md}{packet proof}
retains the exact frozen odd-N family and establishes
\(|\operatorname{Tr}U_N^j|=O_j(1)\) for every fixed nonzero integer j.
The method is standard finite-time coherent propagation, reconstructed
with the exact ordinary Weyl symbol and boundary character.

For z=(q,p), the frame is
\[
\psi_{z,N}(x)=\left(\frac2N\right)^{1/4}\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}
 e^{-\pi N(x/N-q-k)^2}e^{2\pi iNp(x/N-q-k)},
\qquad N\int|\psi_{z,N}\rangle\langle\psi_{z,N}|dz=I.
\]
The p integral sets x=y,k=l; the remaining Gaussian integral is exactly
1/N. Odd midpoint Weyl sampling, the invariant lattice character under
S0 mod2, and clock/shift irreducibility identify the actual matrix M\_N.
A degree-five triangular packet expansion has residual O(h\^{}4); sampling
that weighted-Schwartz residual before finite-dimensional Duhamel gives
error O(h\^{}3). Its overlap with the original packet is bounded by
\(C_{j,M}(1+\operatorname{dist}(F^jz,z)/\sqrt h)^{-M}+C_jh^3\).
Anosov nondegeneracy of fixed-time periodic points gives sublevel area
O\_j(r\^{}2), and the exact frame trace gives O\_j(Nh)=O\_j(1).
One-step Egorov or a first-order Gaussian approximation alone would not
justify this bound. Keeping the leading Gaussian gives the explicit
fixed-time limsup upper bound
\[
\sqrt2\sum_{z\in\operatorname{Fix}(F^j)}
\frac{\det(I+DF^j(z)DF^j(z)^{\mathsf T})^{1/4}}
{|\det(DF^j(z)-I)|}.
\]
Localized higher packets contribute O(sqrt(h)) after the trace integral;
the norm remainder contributes O(Nh\^{}3). The classical derivative bound
and the 4/32 fixed-point counts yield eventual
\(|\operatorname{Tr}U_N|<4\), \(|\operatorname{Tr}U_N^2|<9\) and sum below 13.
Thus K=20 is available. No effective dimension threshold or estimate
with j of order N is supplied.

FM-007 had already proved normalized fixed-time traces tend to zero in
an actual logarithmic time window. The new bounded unnormalized input
improves the starting FLOW-003 covariance rate to \textbar m2\textbar=O(1/N), and closes
the fixed-trace boundedness assumptions, with subsequences for convergence
of the initial traces. It does not remove the external noise.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/egorov_overlap_rigidity.md}{Egorov overlap lemma} states that if two
fixed quantized classical maps F,G coincide on area zero, then
\[
N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(K_N^*L_N)\to0,\qquad
\inf_{|\zeta|=1}N^{-1/2}\|K_N-\zeta L_N\|_{HS}\to\sqrt2.
\]
If the maps differ at one point, the operator-norm liminf is at least
sqrt(2), by localized coherent states. The four actual fixed-point
Hessians show every fixed nonzero power remains non-affine under C1
conjugacy. Fixed smooth conjugators therefore give the operator separation;
fixed analytic ones also give the HS separation. N-dependent spectral
basis changes are outside these assertions.

\hypertarget{coherent-words-despite-auxiliary-expansion}{%
\subsection{Coherent words despite auxiliary expansion}\label{coherent-words-despite-auxiliary-expansion}}

\textbf{Claim ID:} \texttt{BGS-TRACE-013}. The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/mathematics/arithmetic_word_expansion_obstruction.md}{complete counterexample}
uses three fixed integral hyperbolic matrices
\[
R=\begin{pmatrix}4&9\\19&43\end{pmatrix},\quad
S=\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\1&1\end{pmatrix},\quad
V=\begin{pmatrix}-5&19\\-24&91\end{pmatrix},\quad VS=R.
\]
R has no integer/topological root and no topological reversor. The proofs
exhaust determinant signs and use incompatible modulo-three/seven Lucas
periods, respectively. The rational fourth root (R+8I)/21 gives
\(d_p=\operatorname{ord}_pR\mid(p-1)/4\) for all primes p=1 mod20.
Thus the even Weil sector of odd dimension N=(p+1)/2 has a clock of
unfolded pitch N/d\textgreater2, failing Sine2 and its weak local law.

The non-elementary fixed generators S,V have a uniform Cayley gap by
Bourgain--Gamburd. Representation transfer and even-sector irreducibility
therefore give a uniform one-copy quantum mixing gap. Yet its two-copy
invariant rank is D2=(p+7)/4, not the Haar rank two. More generally
\[
D_{k,p}=\frac{2((p+1)/2)^{2k}+(p-3)p(p+1)/2
 +(p^2-1)2^{1-2k}\sum_{l=0}^k\binom{2k}{2l}p^l}{p(p^2-1)}.
\]
The character/frame-potential method is prior Gross--Audenaert--Eisert
mathematics. The complete class calculation gives extensive invariant
memory and, for k\textgreater=3, D\_k\textasciitilde N\^{}(2k-3)/4.

On the full p-space the symplectic two-copy invariant rank is 2p+1.
Adding a fixed Weyl translation only to the auxiliary channel leaves I
and swap, and compresses every other orbit by -1/(p\^{}2-1). A two-case
Dirichlet argument gives a uniform two-copy gap gamma/18. This channel
mixes parity; the added translation never enters the selected word VS.
It therefore excludes a full-space auxiliary-gap sufficiency criterion,
without asserting a sector-preserving two-copy counterexample.

Label an algebraic eigenbasis of rho(R) by j=1,\ldots,p and perturb by
\(D_p=\exp(iA_p/p!)\), \(A_p=\sum_j(j/p)|\psi_j\rangle\langle\psi_j|\).
Hermite--Lindemann proves simple spectra, nonzero traces of every positive
power and absence of scalar powers. The perturbation is analytic flat
on each fixed strip; the enlarged two-copy gap remains gamma/36.
Nevertheless, for the even sector,
\[
N^{-2}\sum_{\substack{N\le m\le2N\\d_p\mid m}}
 \left||\operatorname{Tr}((D_p\rho(R))^m)|^2-N\right|\ge2-o(1).
\]
The full p-space lower bound is 4-o(1). At every fixed nonzero time,
the regular Weil character and flat perturbation give bounded traces
1+o(1). Thus all these exact exclusions, fixed-time bounds and auxiliary
gaps coexist with coherent Heisenberg returns. Fixed nonlinear shear
conjugation preserves the joint construction, but retains smooth
arithmetic conjugacy. Earlier project nonlinear arithmetic examples
are credited. This is a different map, not an obstruction established
for the frozen operator.

The \href{https://github.com/ChurilovMaksim/BGS/blob/main/record/expansion_wavepacket_review_20261004.md}{current research audit}
records exact rational/modular controls, finite character and channel tests,
odd coherent frames, checked source leaves and prior-scope comparison.
The actual frozen block mass, shifted microscopic energy and nonresonant
signed hierarchy remain unproved.

\hypertarget{verification-and-remaining-work}{%
\subsection{Verification and remaining work}\label{verification-and-remaining-work}}

The recovered supplement includes exact arithmetic replay, an independent
C++ verifier, independent matrix assemblies and numerical identity checks.
The new quartic relation was checked in 27 finite cases and by a separate
internal algebra audit. Its source code and proof are retained. Auxiliary
kick strengths in these tests do not resolve \(\tau=10^{-80}\).

The Lean module \texttt{CueLoopKernels} states the cubic positive-part identity
and a cleared-denominator elimination kernel over integers. These are a
small algebraic layer; they do not formalize the analytic loop criterion.
Current compilation results are recorded in the publication review.

The remaining task is a model-specific Heisenberg-scale cancellation
estimate for the actual mixed resolvent products, or an equally strong
direct trace comparison. No noise approximation, source theorem or finite
computation in this chapter supplies that missing estimate.
